title: First 120: Role Evidence Canvas & Buddy Slate
body:
Purpose and scope:
This document provides a compact, role‑driven evidence canvas and an associated "buddy slate" to guide the first 120 days for new hires. The goal is threefold: (1) give managers a concise activation plan with observable artifacts, (2) give interviewers a calibrated evidence rubric to validate offers and early success, and (3) give new hires a clear checklist of learning and ownership milestones.

Why this is different:
- Focus on evidence (deliverables/artifacts) rather than vague activities.
- Role‑specific weightings so expectations scale by level (IC2 vs IC4 vs Staff).
- A lightweight buddy roster with explicit responsibilities for week 1/2/4/8/12.
- Short interviewer micro‑probes that map directly to the 14/30/60/90/120 artifacts used for evaluation.

How to use this canvas:
- Hiring: interview panels use the same evidence items (with pre‑assigned weights) to decide on offer consistency.
- Onboarding: manager and buddy use the canvas to assign initial tasks and sign off on artifacts.
- Calibration: people‑ops runs a 1‑hour quarterly rubric calibration using recorded examples linked below.

1) Role Evidence Canvas (template)
- Role name: [e.g., Serving Runtime Engineer]
- Level: [IC2 / IC3 / IC4 / Staff]
- Primary outcome (120d): [e.g., Shipping a KV cache optimization that reduces median latency by >=6% in a canary].
- 14d artifacts (observable): [access granted, infra dev laptop configured, readme of core repo, first small bug fix PR]
- 30d artifacts: [owned feature spike doc, two PRs merged, first oncall shift buddyed]
- 60d artifacts: [validated perf test run, customer‑impacting postmortem participation, mentorship of a new hire demo] 
- 90d artifacts: [feature ownership handoff, rollout playbook, post‑deployment metrics dashboard configured]
- 120d artifacts (exit criteria): [demonstrated SLA ownership, independent deploys to staging, proposal for next quarter work].
- Quality signals (what success looks like): [code review feedback closed <48h, test coverage for owned modules > 70%, runbook completeness score > 4/5]
- Risks/unknowns to de‑risk: [missing infra keys, region limits, blocked PRs]

2) Weighting matrix (examples; adjust per ladder)
- Core technical delivery: 40%
- Operational reliability / oncall performance: 20%
- Collaboration & communication (docs, async updates): 15%
- Mentorship / team uplift: 10%
- Product impact (measurable customer metrics): 15%

Mapping by level (quick guide):
- IC2: technical delivery 55%, operations 15%, collaboration 20%, mentorship 5%, product 5%
- IC3: technical 45%, operations 20%, collaboration 15%, mentorship 10%, product 10%
- Staff: technical 30%, operations 25%, collaboration 15%, mentorship 20%, product 10%

3) Buddy Slate (week windows and responsibilities)
- Primary buddy (week 0–2): orient access, repo walkthrough, first PR help, daily check‑ins
- Secondary buddy (week 3–6): architecture walkthroughs, pairing on oncall tasks, review of 30d spike
- Metrics buddy (week 6–12): dashboard coaching, SLO tuning, rollout checklist signoff
- Peer mentor (ongoing): career path conversation, cross‑team intro, demo attendee

Buddy quick checklist (first 7 days):
- Confirm SSO/KMS/role permissions (security ops ticket ID)
- Run local dev environment with sample load test in <2 hours
- Open first PR with minimal change and get 1 reviewer assigned
- Add to oncall rotation shadow calendar and pager test run

4) Interviewer micro‑probes (for panels and take‑homes)
These are short, repeatable evidence probes that map to the canvas artifacts. Interviewers should record both the probe result and which canvas artifact it validates. Use the weighting matrix to score.
- Probe A: Read a short spike doc and identify missing risk mitigations (maps to 30d artifact). 12 minutes.
- Probe B: Given a small simulated perf regression, sketch a triage sequence and a mitigation plan (maps to 60d artifact). 18 minutes.
- Probe C: Code pair on a tiny refactor that improves testability; measure test ownership and PR hygiene (maps to 14/30d artifacts). 30 minutes.
- Probe D: Ask candidate to write the headline and three metrics they’d watch after deploying a change (maps to 90/120d product impact). 8 minutes.

Scoring guidance (panel):
- Each probe scored 1–4 with anchors: 1 = missing, 2 = partial, 3 = solid, 4 = above expectations.
- Convert probe scores into evidence items per canvas and apply level weighting.
- Interviewer note: prefer short concrete examples over hypothetical abstractions.

5) Manager checklist for 0–30–60–90–120 day reviews
- Day 0–7: access verified, buddy assigned, one tangible PR merged, calendar of check‑ins set.
- Day 14: 14d artifacts reviewed; if any core artifact missing, raise remediation plan within 3 days.
- Day 30: 30d artifacts validated, oncall buddy finished, manager provides documented feedback.
- Day 60: Cross‑functional demo scheduled, metrics reviewed, remediation closed or extended.
- Day 90: Formal 90d calibration note written and shared with people‑ops; decision on extension/leveling if necessary.
- Day 120: Exit criteria evaluated; if met, new hire moved to steady‑state plan and given ownership area.

6) Sample probes for Serving Runtime Engineer (concrete examples)
- 14d: Small PR to improve logging for `kv_cache` hot key path and a unit test that reproduces previous flakiness.
- 30d: Spike doc comparing three kernel choices for 8k context models; one recommendation with cost/latency tradeoffs.
- 60d: Canary deployment of a micro‑optimization with a before/after latency table and a rollback plan.

7) Security & Compliance onboarding addenda
- People‑ops must confirm that KMS access request ID and audit log export enabled before any private dataset is accessed.
- Compliance buddy signs off on data handling checklist during week 1.

8) Handoff artifacts and where to store them
- Place spike docs in /docs/onboarding/<hire-name>-spikes.md
- PR links and perf dashboards attached to the hire’s onboarding ticket (JIRA)
- Runbooks go to the runbook repo with a PR labeled `onboarding/<hire-name>`

9) Feedback timeline and normalization rule
- Interview feedback due within 48 hours; if any interviewer misses this, people‑ops prompts and auto‑sends a short form to capture top 3 signals.
- Normalization: when panel variance > 1.0 on the 1–4 scale, run a 20‑minute calibration huddle and re‑score.

10) Calibration workshop (quarterly)
- 60 minutes: 10 min intro, 25 min review of 3 anonymized hires (examples and scores), 15 min alignment and rule updates, 10 min action items.

Open questions / follow‑ups:
- Do we want separate canvases for Customer Success and Solutions Eng (they need customer demos as exit artifacts)? Suggest a follow‑up to template a non‑engineering canvas.
- Should we link to short recorded exemplar interviews for staff vs IC3 examples (people‑ops to curate).

Appendix: short templates
- 14d signoff snippet (copy into JIRA comment): "14d signoff: access verified (IDs: ___), first PR merged (link), buddy notes: ___. Manager: ___."
- Manager note template for 90d (copyable): "90d review: artifacts validated: [list]. Risks remaining: [list]. Suggested extensions/leveling: [recommendation]."
